source: Fragmenta in epistulam ad Galatas (in catenis) Gal: Prolog Τοῦ κηρύγματος εἰς τὰ ἔθνη δεχθέντος τινὲς τῶν ἀπὸ τῆς περιτομῆς ἐξιόντες ἔπειθον τὰ ἔθνη ἰουδαΐζειν, καὶ πρώτη περὶ τούτου φαίνεται ζήτησις γεγενημένη ἐν Ἀντιοχείᾳ, ὅτι οἱ ἀπόστολοι ἔγραψαν μὴ ὑποκεῖσθαι νόμῳ, ἀπέχεσθαι δὲ εἰδωλοθύτου καὶ αἵματος καὶ πνικτοῦ καὶ πορνείας· οὕτω γὰρ ἔδοξε τῷ ἁγίῳ πνεύματι. ἐκράτησε δὲ τὸ νόσημα τοῦτο τῶν Galατῶν συμφώνως ἰουδαΐζειν βουληθέντων. ἐπείσθησαν δὲ ὑπὸ τῶν διαστρεφόντων λεγόντων, ὡς οἱ λοιποὶ ἀπόστολοι οὐ κωλύουσι τοὺς βουλομένους τηρεῖν τὸν νόμον. 299 Gal 1,4 ∆είκνυσιν ὅτι οὐ Μωϋσῆς ἀπέθανεν ὑπὲρ τοῦ κόσμου οὐδέ τις τῶν προφητῶν ἄλλος. οὐ δεῖ τοίνυν ἡττᾶσθαι τοῦ μὴ σώσαντος, ἀλλὰ τοῦ ὑπὲρ ἡμῶν ἀποθανόντος. Gal 1,6–7 Εἰς ἕτερον εὐαγγέλιον ὃ οὐκ ἔστιν ἕτερον, φησίν· τὸ γὰρ ἡμέτερον εὐαγγέλιον καὶ τὸ τῶν ἀποστόλων ἐκτὸς ὑμᾶς εἶναι βούλεται νόμου. Gal 1,8–10 Ἔστω ἄγγελος, διὰ τί δὲ καὶ ἡ μεῖς; ὅτε ἐκηρύττομεν, πνεύματος ἁγίου δυνάμει ἐκηρύξαμεν· τὸ δὲ πνεῦμα τὸ ἅγιον οὐ μετανοεῖ. ἐὰν οὖν ἄλλα εἴπωμεν, κατελίπομεν τὰ τοῦ πνεύματος. ἔστω οὖν καὶ ὁ κῆρυξ ἀνάθεμα, ἀθετῶν τὸ κήρυγμα. Παρ' ὃ παρελάβετε. οὐκ ἐκήρυξα μὲν ἐγώ, φησίν, ὑμεῖς δὲ οὐκ ἐλάβετε, ἀλλὰ καὶ ἐγὼ ἐκήρυξα, καὶ ὑμεῖς παρελάβετε. οὔτε ἐγὼ μετανοῶ κηρύξας, καὶ ὑμεῖς τηρήσατε ὃ εἰλήφατε. Ἄρτι γὰρ ἀνθρώπους πείθω ἢ τὸν θεόν; ἢ ζητῶ ἀνθρώποις ἀρέσκειν; εἰ ἔτι ἀνθρώποις ἤρεσκον, Χριστοῦ δοῦλος οὐκ ἂν ἤμην. μέλλων αὐτοὺς ὑπομιμνήσκειν τοῦ ἰδίου εὐαγγελίου, προλαβὼν ἀσφαλίζεται ἵνα μὴ νομίσωσιν ὅτι θεραπεύει ὑπαγόμενος· ἐπιπλήττει γὰρ νουθετῶν. εἰπὼν δὲ εἰ ἔτι, ἐδήλωσεν ὅτι ἤρεσκε ποτὲ ἀνθρώποις. τίσι δὲ ἤρεσκεν; παρ' ὧν ἔλαβεν ἐπιστολὰς τοὺς εἰς ∆αμασκὸν πιστοὺς κακῶσαι. εἰ οὖν, φησίν, ἤρεσκον ἔτι τοῖς Ἰουδαίοις, οὐκ ἂν ἐπίστευσα τῷ Χριστῷ. Gal 1,13 Τίς χρεία τῆς ἐν τῷ Ἰουδαϊσμῷ ἀναστροφῆς ἀλλ' ἵνα δείξῃ, ὅτι οὐ προλήψει δουλεύει ἀλλ' ἀληθείᾳ· οὐ γὰρ μισήσας τὸν νόμον ὑπέδραμε τὴν χάριν–ἐξεδίκει γὰρ αὐτόν–ἀλλ' εὑρὼν τὸ τέλειον ἀπέστη τοῦ νόμου. Νῦν δείκνυσιν ὅτι πλέον τι τῶν περὶ Πέτρον ἔχει· οὐ γὰρ ἐζήλωσαν ἐκεῖνοι ὑπὲρ τοῦ Ἰουδαϊσμοῦ ἀπειθοῦντες τῷ Χριστιανισμῷ ὡς ἐγώ. 300 μὴ τοίνυν οἰηθῇτε ὅτι μισήσας τὸν νόμον ἦλθον εἰς τὴν χάριν– ἐξεδίκουν γὰρ τὸν νόμον–ἀλλ' εὗρον τὸ τέλειον, καὶ οὐκ ἐξισῶ τὸν νόμον τῇ τελείᾳ χάριτι. Gal 1,16 Οὐ διαβάλλων δὲ τοὺς ἀποστόλους τοῦτό φησιν, ἀλλ' ὅτι οὐκ ἐστοίχησα θνητῇ σαρκί. Gal 2,16 Εἰ γὰρ ἐξ ἔργων οὐδεὶς δικαιοῦται τῶν πόνον φερόντων, ἐκ δὲ πίστεως ὅπου τὸ τῆς εὐκολίας καὶ τὸ τῆς δικαιοσύνης μέγα, πῶς οὐκ ἀναγκαῖόν φησιν ἐάσαντας νόμον ἀρκεῖσθαι τῇ χάριτι; ἐξ ἔργων νόμου λέγει μὴ δικαιοῦσθαι, οὐκ ἐξ ἐντολῶν· ἡ γὰρ ἐντολὴ δικαιοῖ ἀκουομένη, τὸ δὲ ἔργον ἦν τὸ δυσκατόρθωτον.
english: When the preaching had been received among the nations, some from the circumcision party went out and persuaded the nations to judaize. The first dispute about this appears to have arisen in Antioch, because the apostles wrote that they should not be subject to the law, but should abstain from idol-sacrifice, blood, what is strangled, and sexual immorality; for so it seemed good to the Holy Spirit. This disease took hold of the Galatians, who willingly agreed to judaize. They were persuaded by those who distort the gospel, who said that the other apostles do not prevent those who wish to keep the law.
He shows that Moses did not die for the world, nor did any other of the prophets. Therefore we must not be mastered by the one who did not save, but by the one who died for us.
"To a different gospel," he says, "which is not another." For our gospel and that of the apostles wants you to be outside the law.

"Even if an angel"—but why also we? When we preached, we preached in the power of the Holy Spirit; and the Holy Spirit does not change his mind. If then we say other things, we have abandoned the things of the Spirit. So let even the herald be anathema if he rejects the proclamation.
"Contrary to what you received." It is not that I preached, he says, and you did not receive; but I preached, and you received. Neither do I repent of having preached, and you—keep what you received.

"Am I now persuading people or God? Or do I seek to please people? If I were still pleasing people, I would not be a servant of Christ." Since he is about to remind them of his own gospel, he secures himself in advance so that they will not think he is currying favor because he is being manipulated; for he rebukes while admonishing. By saying "if still," he showed that he once pleased people. Whom did he please? Those from whom he received letters to harm the faithful in Damascus. If then, he says, I were still pleasing the Jews, I would not have believed in Christ.

What need is there for his former conduct in Judaism? It is to show that he is not enslaved to prejudice but to truth. For he did not hate the law and run to grace—he was defending it—but he found what is perfect and departed from the law.

Now he shows that he has something more than those around Peter. For they did not burn with zeal for Judaism in disobedience to Christianity, as I did. Do not think, then, that I hated the law and came to grace—I was defending the law—but I found what is perfect, and I do not make the law equal to the perfect grace.
He does not say this to slander the apostles, but because I did not follow mortal flesh.

For if no one is justified by works, which bring toil, but by faith, where there is ease and the greatness of righteousness, how is it not necessary, he says, to leave the law and be content with grace? He says one is not justified by works of the law, not that one is not justified by commandments; for a commandment justifies when it is heard, but the work was what was hard to achieve.

findings.checker_says: Glossary requires 'works of the law', not bare 'works'.
findings.reviewer_note: Source at this point is bare ἐξ ἔργων; the English already says 'works of the law' where νόμου appears. Glossary rule misapplied.

findings.checker_says: Glossary requires 'works of the law', not bare 'works'.
findings.reviewer_note: ἔργων has no νόμου here; 'works' is exact. Forcing 'of the law' would add content.
ἐντολῶν is plural; 'commandments' is correct. Glossary does not govern grammatical number.

findings.checker_says: Glossary requires 'commandment', but this is singular; however 'commandments' above breaks glossary.

findings.quote: because I did not follow mortal flesh
findings.checker_says: English 'I' makes Paul the speaker, but source has Eusebius commenting with third-person reference.
findings.reviewer_note: ὅτι is recitative (Paul's voice reported), not causal; 'because I did not' makes the commentator the 'I'.

findings.quote: because I did not follow mortal flesh
findings.checker_says: The English 'I' confuses Eusebius's comment about Paul with Paul's own words; Eusebius speaks in third person.
'Manipulated' suggests external control; ὑπαγόμενος here means 'yielding/going along' or 'being submissive', not manipulation.
findings.reviewer_note: ὑπαγόμενος = being led on/induced; 'manipulated' is within range and 'yielding' is no more accurate.

findings.quote: because I did not follow mortal flesh
findings.checker_says: This is the key error: source has third-person comment by Eusebius (οὐκ ἐστοίχησα is part of Paul's own statement in indirect discourse? No—looking again: 'Οὐ διαβάλλων δὲ τοὺς ἀποστόλους τοῦτό φησιν, ἀλλ' ὅτι οὐκ ἐστοίχησα θνητῇ σαρκί.' This is Eusebius explaining what Paul means. The ἐστοίχησα is first person because it's Paul's own words being explained. But Eusebius introduces it with 'φησιν'—he says. So the English 'I' would be wrong because Eusebius is commenting, not quoting Paul directly. The 'I' in the source is Paul's voice embedded in Eusebius's comment. However, the English 'because I did not follow' makes Eusebius speak as if he were Paul, which is confusing. It should be 'because he did not follow' since Eusebius is the speaker here.
